journey.title: Type a check-in date, then Tab to the guests field
journey.goal: After typing a date and pressing Tab, focus stays on the next field so the user can keep filling the form

functionalJourney.title: Pick a check-in day with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a day fills the check-in date and the guests field still takes input

guards.title: Paging months with the pointer keeps keyboard focus in the date field
guards.goal: After clicking Next month, focus is back in the date field so arrow keys and typing keep working

plan.root_cause: The Pikaday date picker's keyboard handler (_onKeyChange) does not handle the Tab key (keyCode 9). When the picker is visible and the user presses Tab to navigate to the next form field, the picker remains open and the field's blur handler schedules the picker to hide after 100ms. However, focus unexpectedly returns to the date field instead of staying on the next field, likely due to picker hide/show interactions with focus management.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a case for keyCode 9 (Tab) in the _onKeyChange switch statement that calls self.hide() to close the picker and allows the default browser focus navigation to proceed without prevention.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can now tab out of the date picker input field to the next form field (guests) without focus returning to the date field, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Minimal - only adds Tab key handling to close picker. No change to arrow key navigation or date selection.
verification_requirements: Test that pressing Tab on the checkin field moves focus to guests field and closes the date picker.

plan.root_cause: The Pikaday date picker's keyboard handler (_onKeyChange) handles the Tab key (keyCode 9) by synchronously calling self.hide(). This synchronous hide during the keydown event interferes with the browser's default Tab key focus navigation, preventing focus from moving to the next form field (guests). The picker should defer hiding until after the browser processes the Tab key's default focus movement.
plan.repair_strategy: Change the Tab key case in _onKeyChange to defer self.hide() using sto (setTimeout) with 0 delay, allowing the browser to complete focus navigation to the next field before the picker hides. This matches the existing pattern used in draw() for focus management (1ms delay) and _onInputBlur for hide (50ms delay).
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can now tab out of the date picker input field to the next form field (guests) without focus returning to the date field, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order). The picker closes asynchronously after the browser processes the Tab key's default focus movement.
functional_risks: Minimal - only changes Tab key handling from synchronous to asynchronous hide. No change to arrow key navigation, date selection, or other keyboard interactions.
verification_requirements: Test that pressing Tab on the checkin field moves focus to guests field and closes the date picker.
Verify that arrow key navigation within the picker still works correctly.
Verify that date selection still works and closes the picker appropriately.
